# Routbreak

[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/peasantxuan/Routbreak/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/peasantxuan/Routbreak/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![Documentation](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-pkgdown-087a8c.svg)](https://peasantxuan.github.io/Routbreak/)

Routbreak provides tools to quantify epidemic emergence risk in
structured populations using multitype branching processes. `R_ref`
describes the global reproduction threshold, whereas outbreak
probability and `R_ob` depend on the population group in which infection
is introduced.

The package supports Poisson and independent-edge negative-binomial
offspring models, matrix diagnostics, and independent-entry
Poisson–Gamma inference from early transmission data.

## Installation

Routbreak is not yet available from CRAN. Install the development
release from GitHub with:

``` r

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("peasantxuan/Routbreak")
```

## First analysis

Rows of `R` are infection destinations and columns are infection
sources.

``` r

library(Routbreak)

R <- matrix(
  c(
    0.95, 0.12, 0.05,
    0.35, 0.85, 0.12,
    0.12, 0.25, 1.05
  ),
  nrow = 3,
  byrow = TRUE
)

dimnames(R) <- list(
  c("North", "Central", "Coast"),
  c("North", "Central", "Coast")
)

rob_table(R)
```

The returned table contains community-specific outbreak probabilities,
outbreak reproduction ratios (`R_ob`), local and total reproduction
ratios, and the common reference reproduction ratio (`R_ref`).

## Main functions

| Task | Functions |
|----|----|
| Summarize epidemic risk | [`rob_table()`](https://peasantxuan.github.io/Routbreak/reference/rob_table.md) |
| Calculate individual quantities | [`outbreak_prob()`](https://peasantxuan.github.io/Routbreak/reference/outbreak_prob.md), [`r_ob()`](https://peasantxuan.github.io/Routbreak/reference/r_ob.md), [`r_ref()`](https://peasantxuan.github.io/Routbreak/reference/r_ref.md), [`r_local()`](https://peasantxuan.github.io/Routbreak/reference/r_local.md), [`r_total()`](https://peasantxuan.github.io/Routbreak/reference/r_total.md) |
| Import and inspect matrices | [`as_rmatrix()`](https://peasantxuan.github.io/Routbreak/reference/as_rmatrix.md), [`is_irreducible()`](https://peasantxuan.github.io/Routbreak/reference/is_irreducible.md), [`matrix_diagnostics()`](https://peasantxuan.github.io/Routbreak/reference/matrix_diagnostics.md) |
| Scale or construct matrices | [`scale_to_rref()`](https://peasantxuan.github.io/Routbreak/reference/scale_to_rref.md), [`colocation_to_r()`](https://peasantxuan.github.io/Routbreak/reference/colocation_to_r.md) |
| Estimate a matrix | [`infer_R()`](https://peasantxuan.github.io/Routbreak/reference/infer_R.md), [`infer_R_sufficient()`](https://peasantxuan.github.io/Routbreak/reference/infer_R_sufficient.md) |
| Propagate posterior uncertainty | [`estimate_rob()`](https://peasantxuan.github.io/Routbreak/reference/estimate_rob.md) |

For independent-edge negative-binomial offspring, supply
`offspring = "nb"` and the overdispersion parameter `omega`:

``` r

rob_table(R, offspring = "nb", omega = 0.7)
```

## Estimation requires an explicit prior

The Poisson–Gamma inference module estimates directed matrix entries
from generation-resolved transmission links or sufficient statistics.
Users must provide proper Gamma shape and rate parameters. A universal
per-edge prior is not supplied because its implied prior for total
reproduction changes with the number of communities.

``` r

transmissions <- data.frame(
  generation = rep(1L, 4),
  source = c("A", "B", "A", "B"),
  destination = c("A", "A", "B", "B"),
  transmissions = c(12L, 4L, 3L, 16L)
)

fit <- infer_R(
  transmissions,
  initial_cases = c(A = 10, B = 20),
  prior_shape = 1,
  prior_rate = 1.6
)
fit$mle
```

Scalar priors apply to every non-structural edge; matrices allow
edge-specific elicitation. The inference tutorial demonstrates how to
start from a prior on each source’s total reproduction and allocate it
across destinations.

## Documentation

Start with:

- [Getting started with
  Routbreak](https://peasantxuan.github.io/Routbreak/articles/getting-started.html)
- [Function
  reference](https://peasantxuan.github.io/Routbreak/reference/)
- [Practical
  tutorial](https://peasantxuan.github.io/Routbreak/articles/routbreak-practical-tutorial.html),
  including an age-structured Italian POLYMOD application through
  `socialmixr`

Advanced tutorials:

- [Overdispersed offspring
  distributions](https://peasantxuan.github.io/Routbreak/articles/negative-binomial.html)
- [Estimating outbreak reproduction ratios from early transmission
  data](https://peasantxuan.github.io/Routbreak/articles/estimating-rob.html)

The practical tutorial uses `socialmixr`’s Italian POLYMOD survey
interface to estimate a 17-age-group mean contact matrix. Under an
explicitly illustrative uniform per-contact transmission assumption, it
transposes that matrix to Routbreak’s destination-row/source-column
convention and normalizes it to `R_ref = 1.5`. The resulting
reproduction matrix is a teaching scenario, not a directly observed
estimate for an Italian epidemic. Routbreak does not copy or
redistribute the POLYMOD records or the derived matrix; the website
builds the example through the suggested CRAN package `socialmixr`. The
underlying POLYMOD dataset is version 1.1, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.1157934,
licensed CC BY-NC 4.0.

## Assumptions and unsupported regimes

Routbreak uses a fixed nonnegative reproduction matrix during the
stochastic early phase. Outbreak probability is the probability of
non-extinction, not a final attack rate.

Poisson
[`r_ob()`](https://peasantxuan.github.io/Routbreak/reference/r_ob.md)
supports supercritical irreducible matrices, primitive irreducible
matrices at or below threshold through the published continuation, and
diagonal matrices representing independent communities. General
reducible non-diagonal matrices and periodic continuation cases are
reported rather than assigned an invented value. Negative-binomial
[`r_ob()`](https://peasantxuan.github.io/Routbreak/reference/r_ob.md)
requires positive outbreak probabilities because the paper does not
derive its zero-probability continuation.

Matrix inference uses an independent-entry Poisson likelihood with
proper Gamma priors. It is not a negative-binomial likelihood or a
structured model that fixes a normalized mixing matrix and estimates
only a scalar multiplier.

## Citation

The scientific framework is described in:

> Wang B, Valdano E (2026). Redefining and estimating the early-phase
> reproduction ratio for epidemic outbreaks in spatially structured
> populations. *PLOS Computational Biology*, 22(7), e1014425.
> <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1014425>

Use `citation("Routbreak")` for the separate package and paper
citations. Routbreak does not currently have a software DOI.

public repository contains no Italian or Canadian research dataset.

# Package index

## Core outbreak metrics

Introduction-specific early-epidemic risk.

- [`outbreak_prob()`](https://peasantxuan.github.io/Routbreak/reference/outbreak_prob.md)
  : Outbreak probabilities for a spatial branching process
- [`r_ob()`](https://peasantxuan.github.io/Routbreak/reference/r_ob.md)
  : Outbreak reproduction ratio
- [`r_ref()`](https://peasantxuan.github.io/Routbreak/reference/r_ref.md)
  : Reference reproduction ratio
- [`r_local()`](https://peasantxuan.github.io/Routbreak/reference/r_local.md)
  : Local reproduction ratios
- [`r_total()`](https://peasantxuan.github.io/Routbreak/reference/r_total.md)
  : Total reproduction ratios
- [`rob_table()`](https://peasantxuan.github.io/Routbreak/reference/rob_table.md)
  : Summarize outbreak risk by community

## Matrix utilities

Prepare, scale, and diagnose reproduction matrices.

- [`scale_to_rref()`](https://peasantxuan.github.io/Routbreak/reference/scale_to_rref.md)
  : Scale a reproduction matrix to a target reference ratio
- [`colocation_to_r()`](https://peasantxuan.github.io/Routbreak/reference/colocation_to_r.md)
  : Construct a reproduction matrix from colocation data
- [`as_rmatrix()`](https://peasantxuan.github.io/Routbreak/reference/as_rmatrix.md)
  : Convert directed long-format data to a reproduction matrix
- [`is_irreducible()`](https://peasantxuan.github.io/Routbreak/reference/is_irreducible.md)
  : Test whether a reproduction matrix is irreducible
- [`matrix_diagnostics()`](https://peasantxuan.github.io/Routbreak/reference/matrix_diagnostics.md)
  : Diagnose connected components and periodicity

## Statistical inference

Estimate reproduction matrices and propagate posterior uncertainty.

- [`infer_R()`](https://peasantxuan.github.io/Routbreak/reference/infer_R.md)
  : Infer a reproduction matrix from generation-resolved transmission
  data
- [`infer_R_sufficient()`](https://peasantxuan.github.io/Routbreak/reference/infer_R_sufficient.md)
  : Infer a reproduction matrix from sufficient statistics
- [`estimate_rob()`](https://peasantxuan.github.io/Routbreak/reference/estimate_rob.md)
  : Propagate reproduction-matrix uncertainty to outbreak risk
